# The Hermetic PHILOSOPHER,
### Or
# Master Key/
### Of the
### Materials belonging to Chemistry <term>Chymie: In 1709, this term referred to "Alchemy," the pursuit of transforming matter and finding the Philosopher's Stone</term>/ the origin/ and the derivation of all metals and minerals.
### That is:
### A Guide and Summary Account / namely how the Most Universal Supreme <note>original: "Universale Generalissimum"; a term for the "Great Work" or the Philosopher's Stone, believed to be the ultimate substance in alchemy</note>, just as metals and minerals are worked through the Stars <note>original: "Astra"; early scientists believed celestial bodies influenced the growth of minerals inside the earth</note> / finally taking their physical form over many years from water and earth / and being formed into many kinds of shapes / may be attained through Art <note>original: "per Artem"; refers to the alchemist's skill in accelerating natural processes in the laboratory</note> within a short time; and how consequently the properties of all metals and minerals should be most easily investigated and explored.
### Described clearly in many places in this little book for the pleasure of all diligent researchers of Nature/ and consisting of seven small treatises, prepared for printing.

---

->Frankfurt and Leipzig /<-
->Published by Johann Gabriel Grahl/ Bookseller<-
->in Vienna / 1709.<-

<summary>This is the title page of an alchemical manual titled 'The Hermetic Philosopher,' which claims to provide a 'Master Key' to the creation of metals and the Philosopher's Stone through alchemical art. It positions itself as a practical guide for 'researchers of nature' to understand how the stars and elements form minerals.</summary>

## To the Kind Reader. <note>original: "Ad Lectorem Benevolum."</note>

So that you may see the greatest mysteries of the great world,
Read this book of the <term>Art</term> <note>In this context, "Art" refers specifically to Alchemy or the Hermetic Art.</note>, beloved Reader.
You will find in it that which transforms all metals,
And readily turns a heap into gold <note>original: "auriferum." Literally "gold-bearing."</note>.
You will find that by which you may restore human bodies
Pressed by great pain, and relieve weary limbs.

# Preface.

Since this little book <note>original: "Büchlein."</note>, divided into seven small treatises and titled *The Hermetic Philosopher*, is no longer available, and because there has been much demand for it in the meantime, and many lovers of <term>Hermetic Philosophy</term> <note>A philosophical and esoteric tradition based on the writings attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, focusing on the relationship between the divine, the cosmos, and humanity, often through alchemy.</note> have encouraged me to reissue and print it again—especially since the <term>Secrets</term> <note>original: "Arcana." This term refers to the hidden mysteries or specialized knowledge of the alchemists.</note> and leftover secret writings of the ancient philosophers collected in this little book are recommended by the <term>Adepts</term> <note>original: "Adeptis." Individuals who were believed to have successfully attained the highest secrets of alchemy, such as the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> to be read by their close associates—as therein

<summary>This page introduces the book with a Latin poem praising alchemy's power to transform metals and heal the body, followed by a preface explaining that the work is being reprinted due to high demand from students of the Hermetic arts.</summary>

# THE GOLDEN BOOK
### *On the Principles of Nature and Art.*
->Or<-
## A Thorough and Perfect Report on the Manner in Which Metals are Born in the Crevices of the Earth by Nature within their Ores.

Since true and genuine alchemy <note>original: "Alchimie"</note> is a follower of nature—as Albertus Magnus <note>Albertus Magnus (c. 1200–1280) was a prominent German Dominican friar and philosopher; his writings on the natural sciences were so influential that he was often cited as a foundational authority by later alchemists.</note> writes—and since it is entirely derived from and built upon the workings of nature, and is primarily focused on the preparation of things and the revealing of their causes, it is only right that he who does not wish to go astray in this art should correctly understand the state of natural things from their origin and foundation.

It is also necessary that the matter and form <term>matter and form: these terms refer to "Hylomorphism," an Aristotelian concept where "matter" is the raw potential of a thing and "form" is the specific quality or essence that makes it a distinct substance (like gold vs. lead).</term> of these things be very well understood beforehand, for from these two parts all natural creatures derive their essence; and thereafter, one must know the workings of nature upon

...so that he may also be able to conduct and maintain himself according to it.

Now, regarding the first point—the **matter of things**—it is to be recognized, as a universal truth, how the **Wisdom of God** has separated and divided the **circles and spheres** of the whole world into two parts: the **natural world** on the one hand, and the **heavenly world** on the other. The first part is the **circle of the four elements**, beginning at the **Earth** and reaching up to the **spheres of the Moon**, from which point the other world begins, ascending to the **starry heavens**. 

This first world was initially created in a general and unformed matter, such that the Wisdom of God created an unshaped *Hyle* <note>original: "Hyle"; a Greek term used in ancient philosophy to describe primordial, formless matter before it is shaped into specific things.</note> or **Chaos**, about which much has been written by the pagan masters and also the teachers of Holy Scripture. He further divided this matter into four parts and gave each part a specific form—namely, **heat, cold, dryness, and moisture**. Because these qualities and forms, such as heat and cold, are by nature opposed to one another and cannot coexist, they were separated and divided within the aforementioned matter into four parts, called the **four elements**, derived from the matter described above by means of the relationship of heat to cold <note>In the Aristotelian tradition, elements are formed by combinations of these four primary qualities: for example, Fire is hot and dry, while Water is cold and moist.</note>.

For this reason, it is important to note that the male seed alone is the <term>active agent<note>original: "agens." In medieval philosophy, this is the force that initiates change.</note></term>, the thing that performs the work, while the woman's blood is the <term>passive recipient<note>original: "patiens." This is why Aristotle says, in the 20th chapter of the *Book of Animals*, <note>Referring to Aristotle's "On the Generation of Animals," a foundational text for pre-modern biology.</note> that the man provides the "form" and the beginning of the action, while the woman provides the body and the "matter."

It is exactly the same with sulfur and mercury: mercury is the material "matter" of metals, and sulfur is the seed and masculine principle acting upon the mercury. This is because sulfur contains a secret and hidden metallic power within itself; by means of this power—and as is appropriate for the application of heat—the sulfur awakens from within the mercury a unique, agile, and refined <term>sulfur<note>original: "Sulphur." # A Proven Treatise on ALCHEMY, called THE DEFINITION.

->That is:<-
### A True Description of the Excellent and Hidden Art of ALCHEMY.

Definition <note>original Latin: "Definitio"</note> is as much as saying: a description of what the thing is that one desires to know.

The definition of the Art of the Natural Philosophical Secret <note>The "Philosophical Secret" refers to the hidden operations of alchemy, often called the Hermetic Art.</note> is an extraction of the water from the earth, and the leading or bringing back of that same vapor or steam <note>The "shwadem" or "vapor" refers to the gaseous state of a substance during the heating process in a flask.</note> onto its prepared earth; this same earth, with its waters, is cleansed and washed. When it is thus purified with the help of GOD, then the entire mastery <note>The "Mastery" (Meisterschafft) refers to the Great Work or "Magistery"—the successful creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> proceeds to a good conclusion; for first, the water works to <term>dissolve<gloss>original: "solviren." To break down a solid substance into its liquid or essential form.</gloss></term> the earth, so that it

Thus say the old, wise **Philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophi"; referring to the ancient alchemical authorities.</note>: Unless it be the case that you make the **bodies into non-bodies** <note>Transforming solids into vapors or liquids.</note>, and conversely the **spirits corporeal** <note>Turning volatile vapors into a solid, heat-resistant form.</note>, or into bodies, you have not yet found the way or the **rule of the work** <note>original: "Regul des Wercks"; the correct method or formula for the alchemical process.</note>.

### Body, Spirit, Soul <note>original: "Corpus, Spiritus, Anima"</note>

It does not separate from the bodies it has tinged through any strong heat of the fire, so long as they exist and endure.

# Treatise
### Concerning Alchemy and the Stone of the Ancient Philosophers, and how the same is to be prepared; named
# PHOENIX.

The **Philosopher's Stone** <term>Philosopher's Stone: The legendary substance sought by alchemists, believed to be capable of transmuting base metals into gold and serving as an elixir of life.</term> is made from **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio"</note> alone, without the addition or mixing of any foreign or external thing. And **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy, often cited as the primary authority in Hermetic texts.</note>, the Philosopher, says: Fire and **Azoth** <term>Azoth: Regarded as the "universal solvent" or the essential spirit of mercury, it was considered the transformative agent necessary for the Great Work.</term> are sufficient for the **Great Work** <term>Great Work: The "Magnum Opus," or the multi-stage process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</term>, or to make the Stone.

Mercury is born and created by Nature within the earth from a clear and slimy water, united and mixed with a very temperate heat; this occurs in such a way that this union and mixture happens through the very smallest and slightest part, until the moist is tempered by the dry, and the dry likewise by the moist, in equal parts.

# AUTHORITIES OF THE PHILOSOPHERS <note>original Latin: "AUTHORITATES PHILOSOPHORUM."</note>
### That is:
### Various testimonies, reports, and explanations from several famous ancient philosophers regarding the preparation of the **Philosopher’s Stone** <note>original Latin: "Lapis Philosophorum."</note> and its effects.

Here begin the sound authorities and discourses of the ancient sages concerning **natural philosophy** <term>natural philosophy: the historical precursor to modern science, focusing on the study of nature and the physical universe.</term>, from which one can truly recognize out of what and from what the blessed **Philosopher's Stone** is composed and made.

In writing of the works or the labors of **mercury** <note>original: "Quecksilbers"; in alchemy, mercury (or quicksilver) is often viewed not just as a metal, but as a primary "spirit" or principle of all matter.</note>, I have intended to name a Stone of the Philosophers from which true mercury is extracted, which is then transformed into a true **medicine** <note>original: "Medicin"; alchemists believed the Stone was a "universal medicine" that could cure diseases in humans and "heal" base metals into gold.</note>. I do this because the name of this stone is obscured and hidden in all philosophical books.

This Stone now is a blessed mineral stone, a stone of **mercury** <note>original: "Quecksilber"</note> and **sulfur** <note>original: "Schwefel"</note>, just as all other metals resemble it in their nature and **constitution** <term>constitution: the specific mixture of qualities—like hot, cold, moist, or dry—that defines a substance’s character; originally "Complexion".</term>. For that reason, they are also dear and pleasing to one another when they are united or joined together. This occurs because they are **coagulated** <term>coagulated: the process of a liquid becoming a solid or semi-solid mass; originally "coagulirt".</term> and made hard from the same material, and it is only half-cooked. In this regard, there is a difference between this Stone and common red mercury; for its subtle moisture is raised on high from the aforementioned material, and its closest coarse parts are preserved by its moisture. They are thus **thickened** <term>thickened: the process of making a liquid substance dense or solid; originally "inspissirt".</term> and hardened together into a firm and perfect metallic hardness. Thus they are mixed together in a strong union—the moist with the dry—and all these things are lacking in common mercury, which is why it cannot mix or unite itself with the body in the deepest depths of nature.

# Of the Matter, its Pieces and Parts, from which the Stone is Composed and Made.

The composition or preparation of this Stone contains within it two pieces or parts: one is **volatile** <term>volatile: a substance that easily evaporates or escapes into the air when heated; originally "flüchtig".</term>, and the other is **fixed** <term>fixed: a substance that remains stable and resists the transformative power of fire; originally "fix".</term>. Therefore, there must be a middle ground between the **mercury** <note>original: "Quecksilber"</note> and the **metals**. The volatile part, which resembles mercury, the philosophers have called a **spirit** <note>original: "Geist"</note>, and the fixed part they have called a **body** <note>original: "Leib"</note>. For **Alphidius** <note>An influential, though likely legendary, Arabic alchemist frequently cited in medieval and Renaissance European texts.</note> says: The governance and the preparation of the Stone is divided into two parts and in two ways: one is physical and the other is spiritual. The one is generated and comes from the other after the first **conjunction** <term>conjunction: the alchemical "marriage" or union of two opposing substances, such as spirit and body; originally "Conjunction" or "Zusammenfügung".</term>, or joining together, and one is governed by the other. One part is called the **man** <note>original: "Mann"</note> and the other the **woman** <note>original: "Frau"</note>, and these are precisely the works of which the philosophers have spoken: that one accepts the other, one overcomes the other, and one kills the other. And it is to be known that these two parts—namely the volatile and the fixed—are in one thing, from one thing, and of one nature, as **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of the Hermetic tradition and alchemy.</note>, the father of all philosophers, testifies in his *Secrets* <note>original: "Secretis"</note>, and says this truly without lies.

## Certain Testimonies of What Kind of Thing the Philosophers' Stone Is.

It is now held that there is a **Stone of the Philosophers**, about which they have spoken in so many different ways. Through their sayings, they confirm that it is found upon the **mountains**, of which **Morienus** and **Aaron** <note>Morienus and Aaron were legendary figures in early alchemical literature; Morienus was a hermit said to have taught the secrets of the Stone to the Umayyad prince Khalid ibn Yazid.</note> say: "Take the **clear body**, beautiful and new, which is found upon the mountains, and rub it immediately just as it is found in that same hour; and this is the body that does not flee from the fire, and it is a true stone." It is therefore entirely clear and manifest that **red mercury** <note>original: "rothe Quecksilber"</note> is not found upon the mountains, but is instead found in the belly and caverns of the earth, running through all its veins and descending into the deepest pits and caves.

And it is impossible that a **fixed body** <term>fixed body: a substance that remains stable and resists the transformative power of fire; originally "fixes Corpus".</term> (which does not flee from the fire) can be made from it, which **Geber** <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a famous 8th-century scholar often called the father of chemistry.</note> testifies in the chapter *Of the Creation of the World*, where he says: "Mercury, for no reason whatsoever, allows the parts with which it is united in the composition to be separated or divided; rather, its part and entire substance flees from the fire." Therefore, it is quite obvious that mercury cannot be the Philosophers' Stone, as **Alphidius** <note>A frequently cited but mysterious alchemical authority, likely of Arabic origin.</note> testifies when he says: "Our work is a..."

# Now follows further the explanation of the governance and operation of the Philosophers' Stone, from which the Medicine is then made.

To begin with, the order of this book requires—and I have also promised—to teach and explain the **governance** <term>governance: original "Regiment"; the controlled application of heat and specific laboratory procedures over time.</term> and **operation** of the **Philosophers' Stone**, so that the same may be drawn into a true **Medicine**, through which other bodies can be transformed; I have also promised to do this with bright, clear, and explicit words. I have resolved to fully reveal the entire **process** in all its pieces and parts, matching the **concordance** <note>original: "Concordanz"; the agreement and harmony between the writings of different ancient alchemical authorities.</note> of all philosophical texts. I will explain the aforementioned process out of my own free will, so that you shall perceive that according to the teaching of the philosophers, it agrees in every respect. Therefore, it is true that this **Stone** comprises two parts: one part being **volatile** <note>original: "flüchtig"; refers to substances that evaporate or sublime easily when heated, often associated with the "spirit."</note>, and the other **fixed** <note>original: "fix"; substances that remain stable and do not evaporate under high heat, associated with the "body."</note>, with which the effect or **operation** is to begin.

# The third part of this work is the extraction of the subtle soul from the calcined body

## EXTRACTION <note>original Latin: *Extractio*</note>

From this **body** <term>body: the solid, physical remains of the material being worked upon</term>, which is thus destroyed and **calcined** <term>calcined: reduced to a fine powder or ash through intense heat</term>, its subtle substance is drawn out. This substance is called the tinting **soul** <term>soul: the intermediate principle that gives color and transformative power to the alchemical work</term>. Regarding this extraction, Menaldus speaks in the *Turba* <note>The *Turba Philosophorum* (Assembly of the Philosophers) is a famous early alchemical text that records a fictional debate between ancient Greek and pre-Socratic philosophers.</note>, saying: "You should know that the body does not tint <note>original: *färbet*; referring to the power to change the color and nature of a metal</note> by itself if the **spirit** <term>spirit: the volatile, vaporous essence of a substance</term> is not drawn out, which lies hidden in the innermost part of its belly; and there shall be made body, soul, and spirit, which is a spiritual nature in which most wonderful colors appear."

And *Lilium* <note>Likely referring to the *Lilium Alchimiae*, a text often attributed to Arnaldus de Villa Nova or Raymond Lull</note> says: "When the thickness of the body is removed, and the physical nature is broken and scattered for so long until the bodies become non-bodies—that is, until they are entirely dissolved and have become subtle spirits—only then can you extract such a subtle, tinting soul, which lies hidden within the belly of nature. And you should know: if you do not destroy the calcined or dissolved body until you extract the soul from it (which is a **tinting** <note>original: *tingirende*; from the Latin *tingere*, to dye or soak</note> or coloring spirit), then you cannot transform the body with it, nor does the body transform anything..."

The way, then, to extract such a soul is this: Take this destroyed **body** <term>body: the physical mass or material residue left after heating</term>, as was said above, which is body, soul, and spirit. ## On the different colors / which appear in the work of fixation through the rule of the fire

## How Fixation is called a Coagulation of dissolved things.

The **matter** / when the same is spiritual and volatile / then it is called dissolved / as was explained before. ## Secret Book.

# Preface.

I am indeed called **Hortulanus** <term>Hortulanus</term> <note>Latin for "Gardener." CHAPTER I.

# That the Art of Alchemy is True and Certain.

The Philosopher <term>Philosophus</term> <note>original: "Philosophus." Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary author of the Emerald Tablet.</note> speaks truly. For it is true / that the Art of Alchemy <term>Alchimi</term> has been given to us / without lies. He speaks this to refute those / who say / the Art is full of lies / that is / that it is false. "Certainly," he says / that is / found to be so through experience / for what one has tested and experienced / that is certain and true. This is as much as to say / the gold produced through the Art is truly good. And he says: "Most truly" / in the highest degree / for the gold / which is brought about through the Art / surpasses natural gold in all properties / as much in what concerns medicine <term>Artzney</term> <note>Alchemists believed that alchemically "perfected" gold possessed superior healing powers and spiritual purity compared to common gold found in the earth.</note> / as in other things.

### Chapter IV.
### That the Stone has a Father and a Mother, namely the Sun and the Moon, or Gold and Silver.

Just as we see that, in the natural way, one animal begets other animals of its own kind: so also according to the Art <term>Kunst</term> <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy, the "Hermetic Art," which practitioners believed could accelerate or perfect the natural processes of growth and refinement.</note> gold begets gold through the power of multiplication <term>Vermehrung</term> of the aforementioned Stone; from this it follows: Its father is the Sun—understand this as Gold. And because in every natural generation there is required a suitable and fit vessel for the seed, possessing an equality and likeness to the father: so also in this artificial birth it is necessary that the gold have a suitable vessel for its seed and its tincture <term>Tinctur</term> <note>original: "Tinctur." An alchemical substance capable of "dyeing" or transforming base metals into gold or silver.</note>, which accords with it, having an equality with the gold itself; and this is the **Silver of the Wise** <note>The "Silver of the Wise" (Philosophical Silver) is not common silver, but a purified alchemical principle representing the receptive, feminine, and volatile aspect of the work.</note>. From this it further follows: Its mother is the Moon—or Silver.

### Chapter VII.
### On the Purification of the Stone.

Following this, he describes the manner in which the Stone should be multiplied; yet he first establishes the purification of the Stone and the **separation** of its parts, where he says: "You shall separate the **earth** from the **fire** skillfully and subtly, the **subtle** from the **thick** gently, with great understanding"—that is, pleasantly and gradually, not with force but with art; understand: not in haste, but with great wisdom, namely in the **Philosophical Dung** <note>German: *Philosophischen Mist*. This refers to a method of providing a gentle, consistent warmth—often by placing the vessel in a heap of decomposing horse manure—used for the "digestion" or slow cooking of the alchemical substance.</note>. "You shall separate"—that is, **dissolve**. For **dissolution** is a separation of the parts. The earth from the fire, the subtle from the thick—that is, the **feces** <term>feces: the dregs, waste, or solid impurities left behind after a substance has been refined or distilled</term> and impurity from the fire, air, and water, and from the whole substance of the Stone, so that the Stone remains entirely pure and without filth.

### Chapter VIII.

### That the part of the Stone which is not fixed should exceed the fixed part and raise it up along with itself.

After the **Stone** has been thus prepared, it is fit and ready to be multiplied: and then it directs its multiplication and its easy melting <note>German: *Schmelzung*. In this context, it refers to "fusibility"—the Stone's ability to melt like wax and penetrate other substances.</note> into the power to enter both hard bodies as well as soft ones, where he <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary author of the *Emerald Tablet*.</note> says: *He rises from the Earth to the Heaven, and descends again to the Earth.* <note>A famous quote from the *Emerald Tablet* (Latin: *Ascendit a terra in coelum, iterumque descendit in terram*), describing the circulation of the alchemical spirit within the vessel.</note> Here it must be very well noted that, although our Stone in the first work is divided into four parts—which are the four **elements**, as was said above—there are nevertheless only two principal parts. Namely, the one that rises into the heights, which is called the **Unfixed** or **Volatile**, and the other, which remains **fixed** below and is called **Earth** or **Ferment**, which nourishes and ferments the entire Stone, as has been mentioned. However, of that part which is not fixed, one must have a large quantity; and one must, through our **Art**, give it so often to the Stone (which has been made very pure and without uncleanness) until it brings up the entire Stone by the power of the **unfixed spirit**, causing it to **sublimate** <term>sublimate: to heat a solid until it turns into vapor and then collects again as a purified solid in the neck of the vessel</term> and become **subtle**. And that is why he says: *He rises from the Earth to the Heaven.*

### CHAPTER IX.

### How the volatile Stone is to be made fixed again.

After this, one must make this very **Stone**—which has been thus raised or **sublimated** <term>sublimated: heated into a vapor and then solidified again, a process of purification</term>—easily fusible on a **marble** slab with **oil**, or with an **element** that was extracted from the Stone itself in the first work, which is called the **Water of the Stone**. And one must "roast" <note>German: *braten*. In alchemy, this refers to a slow, steady heat applied over a long period.</note> it with frequent sublimation until, through the power of the **fermentation of the Earth** (which was raised up with the "bodies" <note>In alchemy, "bodies" refers to the metallic or solid components of the work.</note>), the entire Stone descends again from **Heaven to the Earth** and remains **fixed**—that is, flowing <note>German: *fliessend*. This is a paradoxical alchemical term; a "fixed" stone is one that does not evaporate in the fire, but it must be "flowing" or fusible like wax so that it can penetrate and transform other metals.</note>. And this is what he <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note> says: *He descends again into the Earth*, and thus he receives the power of the **Upper**—namely, through sublimation—and of the **Lower**—understand this as through the descent. And thus, what is bodily becomes spiritual through sublimation, and what is spiritual becomes bodily in the descent.

### Chapter XXI.
## A Water of Life.

If you wish to make a **Water of Life** <note>original: "Wasser des Lebens"; also known as *Aqua Vitae*, a potent alchemical distillate believed to preserve health and prolong life.</note> for the preservation of human life and to cure all infirmities, proceed as follows: Take a **distilled water** <term>distilled water: Here, "gebrannt Wasser" refers to a high-proof spirit or alcohol produced through distillation.</term> that is very well **rectified** <term>rectified: Purified or concentrated by repeated distillation to remove impurities.</term>. You should not make it into **human blood** <note>original: "Menschen-Blut"; likely a metaphorical term for a specific red stage or consistency in the alchemical process, rather than literal blood.</note> from this, for if it were "human blood," as has been said, it would lose its attractive power—due to the oily nature within the virtue of the herbs—and would lose its entire flavor, and thus would not be good to keep. You should also not use a **burning water** <note>original: "brennend Wasser"; refers to highly flammable, high-strength alcohol (*Aqua Ardens*).</note> for this purpose; the reason being that it would be so strong and sharp that the "burning water" would destroy the entire work, and would also be dangerous to drink. 

Instead, because all perfection of any **Stone** <note>The "Stone" refers to the Philosopher’s Stone, the legendary substance that represents the completion of the alchemical Great Work.</note> consists in the power of its **Earth**, which is called a **nourisher** or **ferment** <term>ferment: A substance used to "leaven" or stabilize the alchemical matter, allowing the volatile spirit to take a solid, permanent form.</term>, as the **Philosopher** <note>original: "Philosophus"; likely referring to the legendary Hermes Trismegistus.</note> testifies when he says: *Its nourisher is the Earth* <note>original: "Seine Ernährerin ist die Erde"; a reference to the Latin "Nutrix eius terra est" from the Emerald Tablet.</note>. Without this ferment, the spirit of the Stone cannot be perfectly preserved, and thus it lacks the perfection of its virtue. Therefore, we give the water the power of its Earth, and then it has its full and complete effect. This is what the Philosopher means when he says: *Its power is perfect* <note>original: "Seine Krafft ist vollkommen"; a reference to the Latin "Vis eius integra est" from the Emerald Tablet.</note>. And when it is turned into Earth, it is then called a **Water of Life**. And so

If you distill it many times from its **Earth** <note>In alchemy, "Earth" refers to the solid, physical residue left after distillation, believed to contain the "salt" or body of the substance.</note>, it will become a **rectified** <term>rectified: purified and strengthened through repeated distillation.</term> and perfect **Water of Life** <note>original: "Aqua vitæ"; a high-proof alcohol or spirit used as a medicinal solvent.</note>.

Beware, therefore, that you do not seek a different Earth, as some wish to do, saying that the power of **tartar** <term>tartar: "Weinstein," the potassium bitartrate crystals that form in wine barrels, often used as a source of "salt" in alchemy.</term> is the Earth of the Stone; some say it is the **dregs of calcined wine** <term>calcined wine: wine that has been heated to a powder; "Häfen" refers to the lees or sediment.</term>; others say it is the **ash of glass** <note>original: "Asche des Glases"; likely referring to potash or similar alkaline fluxes used in glassmaking.</note>. But all of these are in error, and thus one blind man leads the other, and both fall into the pit; for they believe they are making a **Water of Life**, but they are making a **Water of Death**.

For no foreign Earth should enter into it, as **Geber** <note>Geber is the Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–815), a foundational figure in alchemy whose writings emphasized that the "Stone" is found within its own substance.</note> testifies, saying: "It is one Stone, one medicine, to which nothing foreign is added, except only that the superfluous is taken away." Likewise, nothing foreign is added to this **Water of Life**; rather, only all the remaining moisture is removed from it, and that is then the **blessed Stone** <note>original: "gebenedeyte Stein."</note>.

# Bernhard’s Preface.

Study, according to the learned Doctors <note>In this context, "Doctors" refers to the highly educated scholars and authorities of the university and church.</note>, removes ignorance and leads the human intellect back to the true knowledge of all things <note>original: "Studium, secundum Doctores, amovet ignorantiam, & reducit humanum intellectum ad veram scientiam cujuslibet."</note>.

This **Saying** <note>original: "Dictum"</note>, which is not new but has been held in high and certain regard among scholars for a long time, I have wished to recount for this reason: so that I might also add my own humble **opinion** <note>original: "Opinion"</note> to it.

Now, while it is true and undeniable that much trouble and diligence achieve something—and that without preceding effort, little or almost nothing is accomplished—I have nevertheless wished to indicate this to you: that for my own part (leaving every other man to his own head), I concede that such a **Saying** should be held in high enough regard. However, I simultaneously wish to remind and inform you how every benefit with which man is gifted every day, both physically and spiritually, proceeds from God alone. Outside of His divine grace, no one is able—neither through study nor any other practice—to **acquire** <term>acquire: "assequiren," to attain or achieve a result through effort.</term> anything good, much less to bring it to completion according to his will. Therefore, as a preface, I would like to establish the following **Saying** for you as a foundation, and [point] you toward...

...come. If you now read this with diligence and accept it as being meant quite faithfully, you will without doubt not have had this book without profit, provided you follow my advice. If, however, you remain in your own ways and become wise too late through harm—realizing which paths you should have taken—then blame your own lack of understanding and stubbornness, and do not despise other people, since they give you no cause for such contempt. This little book, however, which follows, I divide into four parts.

In the first part, I will speak of the discovery of this **Art** <term>Art: (German: *Kunst*) In this context, the "Great Work" of alchemy—the process of creating the Philosophers' Stone.</term> and of the wise men who, like myself, possessed it and truly understood it.

Yet there are some magnificent <term>intellects</term> <note>original: "Ingenia." For all those to whom they [the masters] granted it, or revealed it as if to their own children, such books of theirs were useful; but now it is a <term>gift of God</term> <note>original: "GOttes-Gab."</note> for anyone who is to grasp the Art from these writings without their direct <term>instruction</term> <note>original: "Information." Finally, having obtained the true <term>Art</term> <note>original: "Kunst." And now follows in the second part an account of which books I also ransacked, and what foolish paths I undertook and walked in this regard, so that seekers may avoid them and instead apply themselves to the true foundation and obtain it. # The Second Part of Bernhard’s Work,
### in which is shown which books he followed, what labor, time, and expense were spent upon them, and what came of it.

After having shown who the first inventor was, and how so many truly and rightfully possessed such a glorious <term>Art</term> <note>The "Art" refers to alchemy—specifically the "Great Work" of transmuting metals or creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, you shall now hear how strangely and wondrously I attempted it before I could come to a thorough understanding of such an art. For the **philosophical conjunction** <term>original: *Philosophische Conjunction*; the fundamental union of opposing alchemical principles.</term> does not happen in that way, and "nothing foreign must be added," as the **Turba** <note>referring to the *Turba Philosophorum* (Assembly of the Philosophers), one of the earliest and most influential Latin alchemical texts.</note> says, and likewise **Geber** <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–815), a famous polymath and the "father of chemistry" whose works were central to European alchemy.</note>: "For there is one stone, one medicine, in which our mastery consists, to which we add no foreign thing, nor do we take anything away, except that which we remove as superfluous during its preparation." <note>original Latin: *Est enim lapis unus, medicina una in quo magisterium nostrum consistit, cui non addimus rem extraneam, nec minuimus nisi quod in præparatione ejus superflua removemus.*</note> Likewise, "Our art does not consist in a multitude of things." <note>original Latin: *Item, in rerum multitudine ars nostra non consistit.*</note> 

Thus, it should have been united differently so that the **active** <term>original Latin: *agens*; the active or "masculine" principle.</term> and the **passive** <term>original Latin: *patiens*; the receptive or "feminine" principle.</term> [elements] might be mixed **through their smallest parts** <note>original Latin: *per minima*; a concept derived from Aristotelian physics suggesting a perfect mixture at the atomic or most fundamental level.</note> and could afterwards generate [the result]. But such a union was not present in the work; and because it was not there, it necessarily follows that nothing came of it. "Since the separation of the active and the passive necessarily ensures that no action takes place." <note>original Latin: *Quoniam separatio agentis & patientis facit necessario, ut non fiat actio.*</note>

For the **perfect bodies** <note>original: *Corpora perfercta*; in alchemy, this refers to gold and silver, which were considered "perfect" because they do not rust or perish in fire.</note>, which are thus simply perfected by nature, are only simply perfect in their own degree. Thus, since one cannot give to another that which it cannot do without itself, that which is in need of aid must remain as it is.

So it is also with the perfect bodies: if they were to share their perfection with the imperfect ones without any intermediary means, they would be worth nothing and would be just as wretched as the imperfect bodies which **Nature** left imperfect. Even though the perfect bodies remain in their perfection, they could in no way do this [give away their perfection], for they are like dead bodies.

Thus, through such fraud, the honest man falls into damage, ridicule, and disadvantage.

Furthermore, when one asks them how they came so easily to <term>the Art</term> <note>original: *die Kunst*; a standard term for Alchemy</note>, they can put forth such **ripe tales** <note>original: *reiffe Weisen*; literally "ripe ways" or "melodies," here referring to their polished, practiced stories</note>—which have not failed them for over a year—and thus run ahead, as has been said, with their villainy to catch many a good, honest...

[Those] fellows who have studied and are well-grounded in their trade, but who solely **out of poverty** <note>original: *ex inopia*</note> must **postpone** <note>original: *postponiren*</note> their studies—[these fraudsters] block every path and bridge to their success with slander and false flattery. This is not just a double **piece of villainy** <note>original: *Schelmenstück*</note>; it also means that the victim—who might have learned something good from an honest fellow and been shown the right path—is instead moved by such "rogue-logic" to follow the fraudster and ignore the other’s valuable advice. And later, when the rogue's advice fails, one can sometimes no longer find those honest people who could have given such good counsel. Therefore, flee the company of such fellows, unless you wish to suffer harm upon harm; for one can never truly know the depths of such men, as their **knavery** <note>original: *Bubenstück*</note> has no end.

That what I have told you is true, I know from experience, because such **gallows-thieves** <note>original: *henckermässige Diebe*; literally "thieves fit for the hangman"</note> harassed me quite boldly; indeed, on account of such wicked boys, I was nearly driven away from the **Art** <note>original: *Kunst*; here referring to the practice of Alchemy</note> entirely and would never have returned to it.

...[so that you] learn to understand what it means to be "reduced to prime matter" <note>original: *in primam materiam reduciret*</note>. You should know that **prime matter** <note>original: *prima materia*</note> does not refer to the four elements <note>original: *vier Elementa*; the basic building blocks of Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</note>, but rather the matter and the thing from which a specific form is made. 

For example, the prime matter of a human is the seed <note>original: *Saamen*</note> of man and woman, mixed and united through a medium. In the same way, the prime matter of metals <note>original: *Metalla*</note> is **sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*</note> and **mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note>, which have been fully cooked <note>a process of alchemical maturation or "digestion"</note> by means of natural heat and turned into metal. Therefore, if metals are to be brought back into their prime matter, they must be turned into sulfur and mercury once again. 

The unwise, however, seek this too deeply; they want the four elements to be the prime matter of metals, which cannot be. For if that were the case, the metals would have to be reduced entirely back to the four elements again. It could then happen that the very substance from which the metal was made—having once been mercury and sulfur—would be completely destroyed and pass into a different being and nature. This would be just as if the male and female seed were destroyed and returned to the four elements; they would then become some other thing. It would be quite foolish to behold: that which should have become a metal, if it were reduced to the four elements, might afterward be made by Nature <note>original: *Natur*</note> into a tree, or an ox, or another thing altogether, because Nature would no longer be bound to specifically generate <note>original: *generiren*</note> metals from it.

# The Third Part of Bernhardus: On the Origin and Root of Metals.

To understand this, it is necessary to know first that God in the beginning made a confused matter <note>original Latin: "confusam materiam"; in alchemy, this refers to the "First Matter" or primordial chaos from which all specific substances were later formed</note>, disordered, which through the will of God was full of many natures; and out of this He drew forth the four elements <note>original Latin: "quatuor Elementa"</note>. From these He made beasts and various creatures: vegetable, mineral, and animal <note>original Latin: "vegetabiles, minerales, & animales"</note>.

Mineral things in general <note>original Latin: "in genere"</note> are composed of earth and water, but the dignity <term>Dignität; in alchemy, this refers to the essential quality, power, or spiritual rank of a substance</term> of the water is more earthy than watery. Within these minerals there are many forms, as you may search for yourself, and which for the sake of brevity I omit from recounting here; and they are multiplied more in that state than in the reduction into their first matter <note>original Latin: "materia"</note>. You should know, however, that the metallic matter is made solely from Mercury <note>original: "Mercurio"</note>, which is cold and moist, and from Sulfur <note>original: "Sulphure"</note>, which is hot and dry. And as I have said that the seeds of all things are composed from the four elements, so too in Mercury and Sulfur there are four elements; and initially domini- <note>The text breaks off here at the catchword; likely completing as "dominating" or "ruling"</note>

Lullius <note>Ramon Llull (c. 1232–1316), a Majorcan philosopher and polymath whose name was frequently attached to alchemical treatises</note>, so it would have to—as will follow—turn out strangely. For the sun is neither hot nor cold in itself, but its motion <note>original Latin: "motus"</note> is naturally hot. Since its motion is guided by the motion of the heavenly bodies, it does not penetrate the earth so steadily that it could heat it; rather, it is the motion that makes it hot. Therefore, it cannot, with its heat—which it does not have from itself but must receive through motion—heat and perfect <note>original: "perficiren"; the alchemical process of "ripening" base metals into gold</note> the minerals <note>original Latin: "mineralia"</note>. For this reason, the heat of the minerals originates from the motion of the sphere of fire <note>original Latin: "motu sphæræ ignis"; in the ancient worldview, the region of pure fire located between the earth's atmosphere and the moon</note>, and the fiery quality they possess within themselves. That their heat and perfection <note>original: "Perfection"</note> cannot come from the sun follows from this: for if this were true, the sun would perfect more in them in 10 years than it does in 5000 years. Since, however, the earth is cold and dry, and the minerals, as mentioned, are in the center of the earth <note>original Latin: "centro terræ"</note>, it would follow that before the sun's heat could penetrate to the minerals so that they were fulfilled and perfected—however small that heat might be—we who must live in the air would die from the heat surrounding us before it reached through water and earth to the mineral deposits. For the coldness of the water and the thickness of the earth would draw the heat to themselves unless it were very strong, and thus no beasts or creatures would be able to live on earth if what they say were true.

# The Fourth Part of Bernhardi, wherein the Practice is set down somewhat Parabolically, &c.

You should know that when I had studied a little, and so much that I believed and felt that I understood something, I then began to seek truthful people who knew such Art <term>Art</term> <note>original: "Kunst"; throughout this text, "Art" refers specifically to Alchemy, the "Sacred Art."</note>; for one experienced man asks another experienced one, and thus one informs the other with a foundation <note>original: "Grund"; meaning a fundamental principle or logical basis.</note>. <meta>This page begins a new section titled "Dicta Alani" (The Sayings of Alanus), attributed to the medieval scholar Alanus de Insulis. It follows the previous page's conclusion of a personal appeal, moving into specific doctrinal instructions on the nature of alchemical transformation and the primary matter of metals.</meta>

->SAYINGS OF ALANUS.<-

# THE SAYINGS OF ALANUS.

Son, set your heart more upon God than upon the **Art** <term>Art</term> <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy, the sacred science of transforming matter and the soul.</note>, for it is a gift from God, and He shares it with whom He wills; therefore, have peace and joy in God, and so you shall possess the Art. For this reason, set a guard over your mouth against the **scoffers** <note>original: "Pitter"; likely a variation of "Spötter," meaning mockers or those who would ridicule the sacred work.</note>. You should not think, when we **sublimate** <term>sublimate</term> <note>A process where a solid is heated into a vapor and then collected again as a solid; in alchemy, this is a method of purification.</note>, that we separate the part that rises upward from that which remains below; for in our **sublimation** <term>sublimation</term>, the fixed parts are not raised, but rather the parts that are not yet fixed are raised. However, we must fix the two together—the **body** <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and the **spirit** <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "Spiritus"</note>—so that they produce an easy flow <note>or "flux," referring to the substance becoming liquid and stable under heat.</note>.

Furthermore, when heat works within moisture, you will first see a **black color** <note>The *nigredo* stage, symbolizing decay and the stripping away of old forms.</note>. Furthermore, when heat works within dryness, you will see a **white color** <note>The *albedo* stage, representing purification and enlightenment.</note>, and within that same white color, the **red color** <note>The *rubedo* stage, the final perfection and the goal of the Great Work.</note> is hidden. Therefore, seekers of the Art of **Alchemy** <term>Alchemy</term> should know that they cannot change the form of metals unless they are first transformed back into their original essence, which original essence is nothing other than **mercury** <term>mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius"; not common quicksilver, but the "Philosophical Mercury" believed to be the root of all metallic life.</note>.

And although many practitioners consider such a restoration of metals into **mercury** <term>mercury</term> to be impossible, consider the possibility that metals were formed in the earth from **mercury** and **sulfur** <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "Schwefel"; according to the "Mercury-Sulfur theory," these two principles combine in different purities to create all metals.</note>; and since **mercury** is the origin of all metals, it is poss- <note>The text cuts off here at the catchword "müg-", which would complete the word "möglich" or "possible."</note>

<summary>This page introduces the "Sayings of Alanus," emphasizing that alchemy is a divine gift. It explains technical concepts like sublimation and the color changes (black to white to red) while asserting that all metals must be returned to their "Mercury" state to be transformed.</summary>

## First Treatise.

1. **On the Principles of Nature and Art <note>original: De Principiis Naturæ & Artis</note>.** A thorough report on the manner in which metals are ripened and born by Nature within their ores in the crevices of the earth, and how one may learn of and recognize the First Matter <note>original: Primam Materiam</note> or the Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: Lapidem Philosophorum</note> from them. <margin>page 1.</margin>

4. Interpretation and observation of the nature of intermediate metals <note>Substances thought to exist between base and noble metals</note> for the transformation of ores in the Art. <margin>31.</margin>
5. How vegetable and animal substances may or may not be brought to a metallic nature. <margin>32.</margin>
6. The <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> of the Philosophers, which all highly experienced philosophers seek. <margin>37.</margin>
